answers.question: What is the Azure resource provider namespace and resource type of an Azure DocumentDB cluster?
answers.answer: Resource provider namespace: Microsoft.DocumentDB. Primary resource type for accounts: Microsoft.DocumentDB/databaseAccounts. (For the newer dedicated MongoDB-style clusters there is also Microsoft.DocumentDB/mongodbClusters.)

answers.question: Which Azure CLI command group creates and manages a cluster? Is it in the core CLI or an extension?
answers.answer: Use the core CLI group az cosmosdb. Example commands: create an account: az cosmosdb create -g MyRG -n my-docdb-account --kind MongoDB --locations regionName=westus. For dedicated MongoDB clusters use the az cosmosdb mongodb cluster subgroup if present: az cosmosdb mongodb cluster create -g MyRG -n myCluster --location westus. (az cosmosdb is part of the core az CLI, not a separate extension in normal installs.)

answers.question: Which Bicep and Terraform resource types deploy a cluster?
answers.answer: Bicep: Microsoft.DocumentDB/databaseAccounts for MongoDB API accounts (and Microsoft.DocumentDB/mongodbClusters for the dedicated MongoDB cluster resource where supported). Terraform (azurerm provider): azurerm_cosmosdb_account for MongoDB API accounts (and in newer azurerm versions there may be an azurerm_cosmosdb_mongo_cluster / azurerm_cosmosdb_mongodb_cluster resource for dedicated clusters).

answers.question: What does a connection string look like: scheme, host suffix, port, and the options it must carry?
answers.answer: Standard MongoDB URI. Example for Azure Cosmos DB (MongoDB API): mongodb://username:password@myaccount.mongo.cosmos.azure.com:10255/?ssl=true&replicaSet=globaldb&retryWrites=false&appName=@myaccount@. The host suffix is *.mongo.cosmos.azure.com, TLS is required (ssl=true), port commonly 10255 for TLS endpoints, and options typically include replicaSet=globaldb and retryWrites=false.

answers.question: How is capacity provisioned and billed: request units, compute tiers with vCores, serverless, or something else?
answers.answer: Two models: for Cosmos DB accounts (MongoDB API) throughput is billed as Request Units (RUs) provisioned at database/collection or using autoscale/serverless. For dedicated MongoDB-style clusters (the managed MongoDB-compatible 'cluster' SKUs) there are compute-tier instance sizes (vCore-like sizing, e.g. M-sizes such as M30) and disk-based billing. Expect RUs for CosmosDB accounts and vCore/instance tiers for dedicated MongoDB clusters.

answers.question: Which authentication methods are supported, and how does a driver authenticate with Microsoft Entra ID?
answers.answer: Primary data-plane auth for MongoDB API is MongoDB credentials (SCRAM username/password) and the TLS-based certificate options where supported. Management/control plane uses Azure AD (Microsoft Entra). There is not a generic MongoDB-wire-protocol mapping for Azure AD tokens in most drivers; drivers authenticate with the MongoDB username/password returned by the service. (If Azure AD integration is required for management, obtain an AAD token and use Azure management APIs.)

answers.question: Which client library should an application use? Is there a service-specific SDK?
answers.answer: Use the official MongoDB drivers (for Python use pymongo or motor). There is no separate service-specific MongoDB driver — you use standard MongoDB client libraries pointed at the service URI. Azure provides azure-cosmos SDK for the SQL/Core API, but for MongoDB API use pymongo.

answers.question: Which vector index types are supported, and what does the command that creates one look like?
answers.answer: The cluster supports vector index types such as DiskANN, HNSW and IVF (as provided by the managed service). The creation is done with a MongoDB createIndex-style call for a vector field. Example (approximate) syntax: db.products.createIndex( { embedding: "knnVector" }, { name: "vec_idx", dimensions: 1536, metric: "cosine", indexType: "hnsw" } ).

answers.question: How are full-text search and hybrid search done?
answers.answer: Basic full-text search uses MongoDB text indexes and the $text operator. For richer/hybrid search (text + vectors) you typically run two queries — a text search ($text) and a vector KNN search (the vector index) — then merge/scoring results in the application. Alternatively, use Azure Cognitive Search connected to the database for advanced full-text and semantic/hybrid scenarios if you need an external search engine.

answers.question: Which MongoDB wire protocol or server versions are supported, and which commonly used MongoDB features are not?
answers.answer: Managed clusters typically advertise a supported MongoDB wire protocol/version (recent clusters can present as MongoDB 7.0). Expect most MongoDB 6.x/7.0 wire-protocol compatibility for drivers. Commonly-missing or limited features: some server-side admin commands, server-side JavaScript ($where), and a few engine-specific aggregation or transaction semantics may differ from upstream MongoDB; multi-document ACID behavior and some change stream semantics can be different or limited depending on the cluster SKU.

answers.question: How do you run the database locally for development and tests: which image or emulator, and which port?
answers.answer: For development use a local MongoDB Docker image matching the target wire version (e.g. mongo:7.0) and expose port 27017. The Azure Cosmos DB Emulator exists for SQL/Core APIs but does not fully emulate the MongoDB API/vector features; so prefer a local mongo container for local unit tests and use the live cluster for vector/index verification.

answers.question: Are change streams supported, and does anything have to be enabled first?
answers.answer: The service offers a change feed-like capability; some MongoDB change stream features are exposed depending on the cluster SKU and MongoDB API compatibility level. You may need a cluster configured with replica-set style behavior (the dedicated cluster SKU) to get full change-stream support. Expect to verify support on your cluster and possibly enable it in cluster settings.

answers.question: Which MCP server gives an agent data-plane tools for this service? Does the general Azure MCP Server cover it?
answers.answer: The documentdb-specific MCP server (named documentdb in the environment) provides the data-plane inspection tools referenced by the sample. The general Azure MCP server covers resource management, but use the documentdb MCP server profile (documentdb/default) to run index inspection and query-plan commands against the cluster.

answers.question: What was this service called before, and how does it relate to Azure Cosmos DB and to the open-source DocumentDB project?
answers.answer: Historically 'DocumentDB' was the original name for what became Azure Cosmos DB (the SQL API). The term 'DocumentDB' as used here maps to the Azure managed Cosmos DB service exposing a MongoDB-compatible API. This is unrelated to any separate open-source project named DocumentDB; Azure's DocumentDB became Cosmos DB and the MongoDB compatibility layer is an API surface on top of Cosmos DB (or on dedicated managed MongoDB-style clusters).

answers.question: What engine is underneath, and does that change anything in application code?
answers.answer: Under the hood it's the Azure-managed storage/compute engine (Cosmos DB or a managed MongoDB cluster implementation) exposing the MongoDB wire protocol. That means application code can use standard MongoDB drivers, but some MongoDB server behaviors, admin commands, and advanced features may differ — test compatibility and indices. Use MongoDB drivers (pymongo) unchanged for CRUD and aggregation, but check feature parity for transactions, change streams and special commands.

answers.question: What index definition does this sample need for vector search?
answers.answer: Create a vector (KNN) index on the embedding field. Example (approximate): db.products.createIndex( { embedding: "knnVector" }, { name: "emb_vec_idx", dimensions: 1536, metric: "cosine", indexType: "hnsw" } ) — adjust indexType to DiskANN or IVF if you want those engines.

answers.question: Which Python libraries will the sample use and how to install them?
answers.answer: Use pymongo for DB access, sentence-transformers (or any embedding provider) for embeddings, and langchain for the agent. Install with pip: pip install pymongo sentence-transformers langchain openai (and any vector model client you plan to use).

answers.question: How should the sample read and use the connection string in code?
answers.answer: Read the MongoDB URI from the environment variable DOCUMENTDB_URI and pass it to pymongo.MongoClient. Example: uri = os.environ['DOCUMENTDB_URI']; client = pymongo.MongoClient(uri, tls=True); db = client['sample_retail_04']. Do not log or persist the raw URI.

answers.question: How will the hybrid search be implemented in the sample?
answers.answer: Rewrite the user query to a search intent, compute an embedding, then run two searches: (1) a vector KNN aggregate using the vector index (e.g. a $search/$knn or createIndex + aggregate with knn stage) to get top-K by embedding similarity, and (2) a text search using a MongoDB text index ($text) or $search. Merge and re-rank results in the application by combining normalized vector and text scores, returning the top matches.

answers.question: What verification and inspection commands will the sample use via the documentdb MCP server?
answers.answer: Use the documentdb MCP server profile to inspect collections, indexes and query plans. Example commands (approximate): mcp documentdb inspect-collections --profile default --database sample_retail_04; mcp documentdb inspect-indexes --profile default --database sample_retail_04 --collection products; and mcp documentdb explain --profile default --database sample_retail_04 --collection products --pipeline '<aggregation-pipeline-json>'.
